questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How the ancient Silk Roads helped world trade to grow
Why so many pubs have closed during the pandemic
A historian's view of coronavirus versus past pandemics
How scientists developed a coronavirus vaccine so fast
questions.why: They hear historian Peter Frankopan's view of the bigger picture of coronavirus versus other pandemics.

questions.q: How does Neil feel about coronavirus at the start?
options: He is fed up with it
He is not worried about it at all
He is excited about the changes it has brought
He thinks it is nearly over
questions.why: Neil says he has really had enough of coronavirus.

questions.q: Why does Georgina think a historian's opinion is useful?
options: Historians understand viruses better than scientists
Politicians have said nothing about the pandemic
Historians can predict when the pandemic will end
It may give a fresh and more hopeful view
questions.why: She says a historian's view might give a fresh look and a more hopeful point of view.

questions.q: According to Peter Frankopan, what is one result of people living close together?
options: Diseases become less dangerous
Diseases pass from animals to humans
People become healthier over time
Trade between countries slows down
questions.why: He says high-density living leads to transitions of disease from animals to human beings.

questions.q: Which example do the presenters give of disease spreading in the past?
options: Cows spreading flu in Asia
Birds carrying disease to Japan
Rats with fleas spreading the plague in Europe
Travellers bringing coronavirus from Wuhan
questions.why: Neil mentions flea-infested rats which spread the plague across Europe in the Middle Ages.

questions.q: Why does Frankopan mention Scandinavia and New Zealand?
options: They have the best-funded hospitals in the world
Being remote means less contact with the world
They were the first countries to get a vaccine
They closed their borders earlier than anyone else
questions.why: He says geographically peripheral places have a different level of connectivity with the rest of the world.

questions.q: Why did the UK catch and spread the virus more quickly, according to Frankopan?
options: It has a very old population
Its government ignored the warnings
Its cities are more crowded than others
It is at the centre of global flight routes
questions.why: He says the UK is the centre of all global flight routes, with many people going in and out.

questions.q: What does Georgina conclude about the current pandemic?
options: It's not so bad historically, and the end is near
It is the worst pandemic in all of human history
It will probably last for many more years to come
It has caused more deaths than the Spanish flu
questions.why: She says far fewer people have died than in earlier pandemics and with a vaccine the end is almost in sight.
